title: Career Roadmap: Data Scientist
summary: A Data Scientist uses statistics, programming, mathematics and domain knowledge to extract insights from data, develop predictive models and support evidence-based decisions.

facts.Current degree: BS (Research) in Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology or Materials

blocks.text: A Data Scientist uses statistics, programming, mathematics and domain knowledge to extract insights from data, develop predictive models and support evidence-based decisions.

For a graduate with a BS (Research) in a natural science or mathematics discipline, this career combines scientific thinking with computational methods. The chosen subject can provide a valuable specialisation—for example, physics for scientific modelling, biology for bioinformatics, chemistry for computational chemistry, mathematics for statistical modelling, or materials science for industrial research.

This is a suggested progression that can be adapted to the actual length and curriculum of the BS (Research) programme.
Stage 1 — Mathematics and programming foundations

blocks.label: Suggested period
blocks.text: First year
Learn

items.text: Python fundamentals, functions, loops, classes and exception handling.

blocks.label: Mathematics relevant to the degree
blocks.text: calculus, linear algebra and discrete mathematics where applicable.

items.text: Probability, descriptive statistics and distributions.
NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib and Jupyter Notebook.
Data structures, algorithms and basic problem-solving.
SQL fundamentals and relational databases.
Git, GitHub and basic research documentation.

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Analyse a scientific dataset from a public repository.
Calculate descriptive statistics and visualise distributions.
Clean missing or inconsistent data.
Write Python functions to automate repetitive calculations.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Analyse a dataset independently and explain the results using statistics and visualisations.
Stage 2 — Statistics and applied data analysis

blocks.label: Suggested period
blocks.text: Second year
Learn

items.text: Statistical inference, confidence intervals and hypothesis testing.
Correlation, regression and experimental design.
Data cleaning, feature engineering and exploratory data analysis.
SQL joins, aggregations and subqueries.
Sampling, bias, missing data and outlier analysis.
Data visualisation and communicating uncertainty.
Scikit-learn fundamentals and model evaluation.

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Analyse a dataset related to your chosen science discipline.
Compare statistical methods for answering a defined research question.
Create a dashboard that explains meaningful patterns.
Document assumptions, limitations and sources of uncertainty.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Produce an evidence-based analysis with defensible statistical conclusions.
Stage 3 — Machine learning and scientific modelling

blocks.label: Suggested period
blocks.text: Third year
Learn

items.text: Regression, classification, clustering and dimensionality reduction.
Decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting and support vector machines.
Cross-validation, regularisation and hyperparameter tuning.
Data leakage, overfitting and appropriate evaluation metrics.
Time-series analysis and forecasting fundamentals.
Feature importance, interpretability and model limitations.
Reproducible experiments, experiment tracking and testing.

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Compare several models against a simple baseline.
Build a prediction model using a domain-specific dataset.
Investigate model errors and the effects of different features.
Use cross-validation and record experimental settings.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Develop and evaluate a machine-learning solution without relying solely on a model's headline accuracy.
Stage 4 — Research specialisation and job preparation

blocks.label: Suggested period
blocks.text: Final learning phase
Learn

items.text: Advanced statistics, optimisation and applied machine learning.
Deep learning fundamentals when relevant to your domain.
Data pipelines, APIs, model deployment and monitoring.
Scientific computing and domain-specific data formats.
Research methodology, reproducibility and technical writing.
Data privacy, responsible AI and ethical handling of datasets.
Collaboration using version control and structured project workflows.

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Complete a substantial scientific data science capstone.
Seek a research internship, industry internship or supervised project.
Present results through a technical report or research poster.
Prepare a portfolio, résumé and technical interview responses.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Demonstrate the ability to turn a scientific or business question into a reproducible data science solution.
The research discipline can differentiate a candidate from general data science applicants.
Physics → Scientific Data Science
Analyse experimental measurements, sensor data, simulations and physical systems.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: numerical methods, uncertainty analysis, optimisation, time series and scientific Python.
Chemistry → Computational Chemistry and Cheminformatics
Analyse molecular properties, experimental chemistry datasets and chemical-process measurements.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: statistics, molecular descriptors, cheminformatics libraries and chemical data interpretation.
Mathematics → Statistical Modelling
Develop predictive models, evaluate uncertainty and solve optimisation problems.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: probability, statistical inference, linear algebra, optimisation and machine learning.
Biology → Bioinformatics and Computational Biology
Analyse biological datasets such as gene expression, genomic sequences and ecological observations.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: statistics, biological databases, sequence analysis, R or Python and responsible biological data handling.
Materials → Materials Informatics
Use data and machine learning to investigate material properties, manufacturing processes and candidate materials.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: feature engineering, regression, optimisation, materials datasets and scientific validation.

blocks.text: Learn the tools that support your research questions rather than trying to master every package.
Projects should demonstrate scientific reasoning, sound evaluation and domain knowledge—not merely the ability to train a model.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Scientific dataset exploration

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Beginner

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Select a public dataset from physics, chemistry, biology, mathematics or materials science. Clean it, explore its structure and investigate a focused question.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: Data cleaning, descriptive statistics, visualisation, missing-data analysis and interpretation.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Reproducible notebook, charts, documented findings and a concise report.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Predictive modelling with scientific data

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Intermediate

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Develop a regression or classification model using a suitable public dataset.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: Baselines, train/test separation, cross-validation, feature engineering, error analysis and appropriate metrics.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Model comparison, reproducible code, limitations and recommendations.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Experimental measurements and anomaly detection

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Intermediate

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Analyse time-series or experimental measurement data and identify unusual observations or changes.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: Data quality checks, time-series visualisation, statistical thresholds and comparison with a simple baseline.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Detection results, false-positive analysis, visualisations and a technical report.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Domain-specific research project

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Advanced

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Investigate a focused research question—for example, predicting material properties, analysing gene expression, modelling a physical process or estimating a chemical property.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: Literature review, domain-informed features, baseline comparisons, appropriate validation and reproducibility.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Research report, source code, data provenance, evaluation results and a discussion of limitations.

For every project, document the research question, dataset source, preprocessing, assumptions, evaluation methods, findings and limitations. Use datasets only under their applicable licences and privacy requirements.
Apply for internships once you can independently analyse a dataset, use Python and SQL, and explain the limitations of your results.

blocks.text: Application preparation

items.text: Build two or three well-documented projects.
Maintain a GitHub portfolio with reproducible code.
Practise statistics, Python, SQL and basic machine learning.
Read research summaries relevant to the target laboratory or employer.
Explain why your scientific subject knowledge is relevant to the position.
Prepare to discuss assumptions, evaluation metrics and model limitations.

rows.text: Practical Python programming and data analysis
Probability, statistical inference and experimental design
Supervised learning, evaluation and model interpretation
Scientific writing, reproducibility and literature review
Bioinformatics, computational chemistry, materials informatics or another relevant domain

blocks.text: Certifications are optional. Choose learning programmes with meaningful assessments and practical assignments rather than collecting certificates without applying the material.

blocks.text: Some specialist positions require a master's degree, PhD, domain-specific training or experience with particular instruments and datasets. Review each job's requirements before applying.
Potential postgraduate directions include:

items.text: MSc in Data Science or Statistics.
MSc in Applied Mathematics or Computational Science.
MSc in Artificial Intelligence or Machine Learning.

MSc in Computational Chemistry.
Materials Science and Materials Informatics programmes.
Research-based master's or PhD programmes in a relevant scientific domain.

blocks.text: Admission depends on the institution's accepted bachelor's qualifications, prerequisites and selection criteria. Verify eligibility before applying.
Stage 1 — Data Analyst or Junior Data Scientist
Clean datasets, produce analyses, build baselines and communicate findings.
Stage 2 — Data Scientist
Develop predictive models, design experiments and support data-driven decisions.
Stage 3 — Senior or Specialised Data Scientist
Own complex analytical projects, mentor colleagues and specialise in scientific or applied machine learning.
Stage 4 — Principal Data Scientist, Research Lead or Analytics Lead
Guide research strategy, technical standards, specialised teams or data science programmes.

Progression depends on technical performance, domain expertise, project impact and available opportunities. Research-focused careers may follow a different path, especially when advanced degrees are required.

A job-ready graduate should be able to:

items.text: Translate a scientific or business question into a measurable analytical problem.
Process and analyse data using Python, SQL and statistical techniques.
Build, compare and evaluate machine-learning models.
Explain uncertainty, assumptions and limitations.
Apply knowledge from their original science discipline to real datasets.
Produce reproducible code, clear visualisations and technical reports.
Collaborate with researchers and business or engineering teams.
Demonstrate practical ability through a portfolio and technical interviews.

blocks.label: Recommended priority
blocks.text: Develop Python, SQL, mathematics and statistics first. Then learn machine learning and build projects connected to the chosen science subject. A portfolio that combines strong analytical methods with genuine domain understanding can help distinguish a science graduate from candidates with only general-purpose data science projects.
